transcript.speech: Replace lost fluids now: water, plus electrolytes if you have them. Get medical help right away for confusion, fainting, no urine, a racing heartbeat, fast breathing, or shock. Other signs: strong thirst, dry mouth, dark urine, dizziness, tiredness. In babies and young children: crying without tears, no wet diaper for 3 hours or more, sunken eyes, unusual sleepiness. Oral rehydration solutions are made for children. Shown first in case someone needs help now. Related: How much water to store, Rationing drinking water, and How long a person can go without water.

message.text: Insulin vials and cartridges can stay unrefrigerated between 59°F and 86°F for up to 28 days and still work. Keep it out of direct heat and sunlight. Don't use insulin that has frozen. transcript.speech: Heat stroke is an emergency: 103°F or higher, hot red skin, confusion, or passing out. Call 911, move them somewhere cooler, cool them with cool cloths or a cool bath, and give nothing to drink. Heat exhaustion (heavy sweating, cold clammy skin, dizziness, nausea): move to a cool place, loosen clothes, use cool wet cloths, sip water. Get help if vomiting, worse, or over an hour. Shown first in case someone needs help now. Related: Rationing drinking water, How much water to store, and How long a person can go without water.

message.text:

Keep generators outside, at least 20 feet from doors, windows, and vents. Don't heat your home with a gas oven. Carbon monoxide has no smell or color, and it kills.
